subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)
description: 100 questions following the real PGP-CET 2025 subject weightage. Mix: 0 easy / 100 medium / 0 hard. Tier is relative: the medium third of the 60 papers by average question difficulty. Every question cites its source.

questions.question: Positive rose water test is suggestive of:
questions.explanation: The Rose-Waaler (rose water) test is positive in rheumatoid arthritis.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: To facilitate wound healing, energy intake should be maintained at about:
questions.explanation: Adequate calories prevent protein from being used for energy in wounds.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Insertional activity is found in:
questions.explanation: Insertional activity is present in innervated muscle.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation O'Sullivan/4th Ed./Pg. 222
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: In lumbar spinal canal stenosis, spinal ______ increases pain and spinal ______ reduces pain.
questions.explanation: Extension narrows the canal and aggravates symptoms; flexion widens it.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: All the following are causes of coxa-vara except:
questions.explanation: Coxa vara (neck-shaft angle below 120 degrees) results from malunion, congenital causes, rickets and osteomalacia, not from hip dislocation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Cervical traction is given for about ______ in chronic conditions such as stiffness.
questions.explanation: Longer, sustained traction helps mobilise chronic stiffness.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Postural tremor is typically seen in:
questions.explanation: Fine postural tremors occur in hyperthyroidism and physiological tremor.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Which contractions increase circulation to the uterus and baby and are experienced in the third trimester by the pregnant woman?
questions.explanation: Painless irregular uterine contractions that become more frequent as term approaches.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: On the dyspnoea scale, a +1 grade is when dyspnoea is:

options.A: Severe so the patient cannot continue
options.B: Mild but noticeable to the observer
options.C: Moderate with the patient able to continue activity
options.D: Mild and not noticeable to the observer

questions.explanation: +1 mild, not noticeable; +2 mild, noticeable; +3 moderate; +4 severe.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: 1 liter of oxygen expanded is equivalent to how much calories?
questions.explanation: One litre of oxygen consumed releases about 5 kcal (4.8) of energy.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: You are treating a patient who is complaining of right shoulder pain. The patient has been diagnosed with a frozen adhesive capsulated shoulder. Which of the following would describe the capsular pattern of the glenohumeral joint?
questions.explanation: The glenohumeral capsular pattern is external rotation, then abduction, then internal rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The formula for duty cycle is:
questions.explanation: Duty cycle is the percentage of the cycle during which the beam is on.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Peroneus tertius is a:

options.A: Plantar flexor and evertor of the ankle
options.B: Plantar flexor and invertor of the ankle
options.C: Dorsiflexor and evertor of the ankle
options.D: Dorsiflexor and invertor of the ankle

questions.explanation: Peroneus tertius dorsiflexes and everts the foot.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A Barthel score of 21-60 indicates:
questions.explanation: Scores of 21-60 indicate severe dependency.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Acute joint inflammation (e.g. synovitis or bursitis) typically presents with which end feel?
questions.explanation: An empty end feel means movement is stopped by pain before any tissue resistance is felt, as in acute inflammation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: In Adams' closed-loop theory, great importance is placed on:
questions.explanation: Adams' theory depends on feedback and the perceptual trace built by practice.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A therapist treats a patient with complete C6 tetraplegia. Which of the following would not be an expected functional outcome for the patient?

options.A: Independent transfers with a sliding board

questions.explanation: Independent bowel and bladder care is not expected at C6.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The postural drainage position for the posterior segments of the upper lobes is:

options.B: Sitting leaning forward over a pillow

questions.explanation: Leaning forward on a pillow drains the posterior upper lobe segments.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The postural drainage position for the superior segments of the lower lobes is:
questions.explanation: The superior (apical) segments of the lower lobes drain with the patient lying prone and flat.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: If the size of the electrode is large, the current density will be ______ and the perception of the stimulus will be ______.
questions.explanation: Large electrodes spread current, lowering density and sensation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The most common type of contracture in a patient with a transfemoral amputation is:
questions.explanation: Hip flexion contracture is the commonest contracture in transfemoral amputation.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Essential of Orthopedicss/Jayant Joshi/Reprint 2009/Pg. 236
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Which current is commonly used for stimulation in Bell's palsy when the muscles are denervated?
questions.explanation: Interrupted galvanic current stimulates denervated muscle.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Volkman's ischemic contracture the muscle commonly involved is:
questions.explanation: Flexor digitorum profundus is the muscle most commonly involved in Volkmann's ischaemic contracture.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: For a chronic condition and/or thick tissue structure (such as the back), the intensity of ultrasound used is:
questions.explanation: Deep, chronic conditions need higher intensities for adequate heating.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: In order to sterilise instruments, the autoclave temperature should be set at about:
questions.explanation: Steam autoclaving at 121 C (250 F) for 15-20 minutes sterilises instruments.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: In Christmas disease (haemophilia B) there is a deficiency of clotting factor:
questions.explanation: Factor IX deficiency causes haemophilia B.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: The hamstrings are mainly responsible for ______ of the swing limb.
questions.explanation: The hamstrings brake the swinging leg in late swing.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Which type of dementia has a sudden (stepwise) onset?
questions.explanation: Vascular dementia progresses stepwise after successive infarcts.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Psychiatry

questions.question: In manual lymphatic drainage, which congestion is cleared first?
questions.explanation: The proximal region is cleared first so that distal fluid has somewhere to drain.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The protein level in a normal urine sample is:
questions.explanation: Trace protein of up to about 8 mg/dL is normal.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: In neutral standing position hip joint is weaker:
questions.explanation: The hip capsule is thinnest anteriorly with the least muscular support in neutral standing.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Kinesiology of MusculoskeletalSystem/ Neumann/1st Ed./Pg. 396
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: You are performing physical therapy in a nursing home where orthostatic hypotension occasionally occurs in some of the elderly patients. Which of the following would not be true concerning orthostatic hypotension?

options.A: It can occur as a result of a patient assuming an upright position
options.B: It is common after long periods of bedrest
options.C: It is common in elderly patients

questions.explanation: Orthostatic hypotension is a fall in blood pressure on standing; it is not limited to 24 hours and may persist.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Physical Rehabilitation Sullivan/5th Ed./Pg. 601-602
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: According to Van't Hoff's law, with every ______ degree Celsius rise in tissue temperature, the rate of cellular oxidation increases ______ times.
questions.explanation: Chemical reaction rates double or triple for each 10 C rise in temperature.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The characteristic of collagen is presence of:
questions.explanation: Collagen is characterised by glycine at every third residue (Gly-X-Y), along with proline and hydroxyproline.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Joint Structure and Function/Norkin/3rd Ed./Pg. 56
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: Which of the following is used to correct club foot?
questions.explanation: The Denis Browne bar holds the feet in corrected positions after manipulation.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: A therapist employed in a nursing home routinely treats patients in excess of 70 years of age. The therapist has noted several consistent postural changes in her patients. Which of the following does not accurately describe the postural changes associated with aging?
questions.explanation: Ageing increases hip flexion (not hip extension), with forward head, rounded shoulders and flexed knees.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Joint Structure and Function/Norkin/Pg. 429-430
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: When a perineal laceration includes only skin, it is classified as:
questions.explanation: First-degree tears involve perineal skin and vaginal mucosa only.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Which of the following are pressure-tolerant areas in a PTB socket?

options.B: Patellar tendon, shafts of tibia and fibula, medial tibial plateau

questions.explanation: PTB loading is through the patellar tendon and the muscular soft tissue along the shafts.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A flat skin lesion of less than 1 cm in diameter is a:
questions.explanation: Macules are small flat colour changes.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: A therapist utilizes resistive testing as part of an initial examination. To assess the C5 myotome the therapist should resist:
questions.explanation: Shoulder abduction tests the C5 myotome.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Orthopedic Physical Assessment/Magee/3rd Ed./Pg. 104
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: A therapist attempts to palpate the peroneus longus and brevis tendons on a patient diagnosed with chronic ankle instability. The facilitate palpation of these structures the therapist should:

options.A: Ask the patient to invert and dorsiflex his foot
options.B: Ask the patient to evert and plantarflex his foot
options.C: Ask the patient to invert and plantarflex his foot
options.D: Ask the patient to evert and dorsiflex his foot

questions.explanation: The peroneal tendons are palpated behind the lateral malleolus during eversion with plantar flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Commissural fibres:

options.A: Connect the cortex to the spinal cord
options.B: Connect the cerebellum to the pons
options.D: Connect different parts within the same hemisphere

questions.explanation: The corpus callosum is the main commissural pathway.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: With heat application, the following decrease EXCEPT:

options.B: Blood flow to organs and resting muscles

questions.explanation: Heat raises metabolic rate while reducing tone and visceral blood flow.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Side lying is advised for pregnant women because it:

options.C: Reduces IVC compression caused in the supine position

questions.explanation: Left lateral position relieves aortocaval compression.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Training intensity is less in:
questions.explanation: Modified CIMT has shorter restraint time and lower intensity than the original CIMT.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Which of the following research designs is NOT quantitative in nature?
questions.explanation: Case studies are generally qualitative.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Sensation over the acromioclavicular joint is tested at the dermatome:
questions.explanation: The AC joint area (tip of shoulder) is C4.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: When a concave joint surface moves on a fixed convex surface, the roll and glide occur:
questions.explanation: Concave on convex: roll and glide in the same direction (e.g. tibia on femur in knee extension).
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: After administration, many drugs are stored at specific locations in the body. What is the primary site for drug storage in the body?
questions.explanation: Adipose tissue is the main depot for lipid-soluble drugs.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: Negativity of resting membrane potential is due to:

options.A: Potassium is more permeable than sodium
options.B: Three sodium ejected for two potassium
options.C: Potassium is brought into the cell and sodium expelled out of the cell

questions.explanation: The resting potential is negative because of high K+ permeability, the Na+/K+ pump (3 Na out, 2 K in) and impermeant intracellular anions.

questions.question: The common deformity seen if the shoulder is involved in a burn is:
questions.explanation: Axillary burns draw the arm into adduction with internal rotation.

questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Earliest sign of Volkman's ischemic contracture is:

options.B: Pain on passive extension of fingers

questions.explanation: Pain on passive extension of the fingers is the earliest sign of Volkmann ischaemic contracture (before pallor and pulselessness).
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Tibialis posterior is a:

options.A: Plantar flexor and evertor of the ankle
options.B: Plantar flexor and invertor of the ankle
options.C: Dorsiflexor and invertor of the ankle
options.D: Dorsiflexor and evertor of the ankle

questions.explanation: Tibialis posterior plantar flexes and inverts the foot and supports the medial arch.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a type of non-probability sampling?
questions.explanation: Cluster sampling is a probability method.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The most common cause of hypogonadism in males is:
questions.explanation: Klinefelter (47,XXY) causes primary testicular failure.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Which cranial nerve moves the adducted eye downward?
questions.explanation: The trochlear nerve supplies superior oblique, which depresses the adducted eye.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Which mineral toxicity leads to Wilson's disease?
questions.explanation: Copper accumulates in the liver and brain in Wilson's disease.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: In Schmidt's schema (open-loop) theory, great importance is placed on:
questions.explanation: Variable practice develops generalised motor programs and schemas.

questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: When the knowledge of participation by the subject affects and influences the results of an experiment, it is called the:

questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Which type of contraction occurs when the force of the muscles is less than the resistance?
questions.explanation: Eccentric contraction occurs when muscle force is less than the resistance and the muscle lengthens.

questions.sourceChapter: Cited reference: Principles of Exercise Therapy/Gardiner/4th Ed./Pg. 22
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A 26-year-old male involved in a motorcycle accident sustains a T10 vertebral fracture. The patient's physician attempts to restrict forward thoracic flexion by using an externally applied device. Which of the following would be the most appropriate selection?
questions.explanation: A thoracolumbosacral orthosis limits thoracic flexion after a T10 fracture.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of type 2 diabetes?

options.D: Autoimmune destruction of the islets of Langerhans beta cells

questions.explanation: Autoimmune islet destruction characterises type 1 diabetes.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The treatment intensity of therapeutic ultrasound is usually:
questions.explanation: Therapeutic intensities are 0.1-3 W/cm2.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Which descending tract controls postural reflexes and muscle tone?
questions.explanation: The vestibulospinal tract adjusts posture and facilitates extensor tone.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Abnormal collagen synthesis is the basic defect in:
questions.explanation: OI results from mutations in the type I collagen genes, causing brittle bones.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Which prosthetic foot permits only sagittal plane motion?
questions.explanation: A single-axis ankle gives plantar flexion and dorsiflexion only.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: According to the ______ theory of development, reinforcement from the environment shapes human motor behaviour.
questions.explanation: Operant conditioning shapes behaviour through reinforcement.
questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of the levator ani?
questions.explanation: Levator ani = pubococcygeus, puborectalis and iliococcygeus; coccygeus lies alongside it.

questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: When the variables fall in a correlation range of 0.26 to 0.50, the strength of the relationship is:

questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The most common injury is a 7 years old child due to fall on outstretched head is:
questions.explanation: A fall on an outstretched hand in a young child most often produces a supracondylar fracture of the humerus.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: A physical therapist examines a patient with shoulder subluxation secondary to a flaccid upper extremity. The therapist's short term goal is to prevent further subluxation. The following techniques would be beneficial in treating the flaccid upper extremity except:

options.D: Arm support when sitting and standing

questions.explanation: Distraction and stretching worsen subluxation in a flaccid shoulder.
questions.sourceBook: Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed., Jaypee 2020)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Secretion removal techniques are often a necessary component of a pulmonary rehabilitation program. Which pulmonary disease is usually associated with a change in the composition of secretions?
questions.explanation: Cystic fibrosis changes the composition of secretions (thick and sticky).

questions.question: Disarticulation of the foot at the midtarsal level is a ______ amputation.

questions.question: If the null hypothesis is accepted (not rejected), it means that:

options.A: There is no relationship between the variables
options.C: There is a relationship between the variables

questions.sourceBook: Khayti Shah, Question Bank for Physiotherapy Licensure and Entrance Exams
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: In normal individuals LDL cholesterol should be less than ______ mg/dL.

questions.question: A therapist designs an exercise program to increase muscle strength and endurance in a patient rehabilitating from knee surgery. Which type of pharmacological agent would have an atagonistic effect on the desired objective?

questions.question: For conditioned people, the ideal duration of a training programme should be:

questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: The ability of a conductor to have electric current induced is known as:

questions.question: An irregular, elevated, transient solid skin lesion (as seen in allergic reactions) is a:
questions.explanation: A wheal is an itchy, transient raised swelling from dermal oedema.

questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The patellar apprehension test, in which the patient tries to contract the quadriceps when the patella is pushed laterally, indicates:
questions.explanation: Apprehension shows a history of lateral patellar instability.

questions.question: A patient with an irregular heart rate is monitored using a single lead electrocardiogram during exercise. Which of the following techniques would provide the therapist with the most accurate measurement of heart rate?

options.A: Count the number of QRS complexes that occur in sixty seconds
options.B: Count the number of R waves the occur in thirty second and multiply by two
options.C: Count the number of P wave that occur in fifteen seconds and multiply by four
options.D: Count the number of T waves that occur in six seconds and multiply by ten

questions.question: Resisted hip flexion tests the myotome:
questions.explanation: Iliopsoas represents L1-L2.

questions.question: A therapist examines a patient with limited range of motion at the glenohumeral joint. Which of the following is considered a capsular pattern of the glenohumeral joint?

options.A: Greatest limitation in flexion flowed by medial rotation
options.B: Greatest limitation in lateral rotation, followed by abduction
options.C: Greatest limitation in medial rotation, followed by abduction
options.D: Greatest limitation in extension and lateral rotation

questions.explanation: The glenohumeral capsular pattern is lateral rotation, then abduction, then medial rotation.

questions.question: A patient rehabilitating from greater trochanteric bursitis completes active range of motion exercises. Which of the following best describes the arthrokinematics associated with hip flexion?

options.B: Anterior glide of the femoral head
options.C: Inferior glide of the femoral head in the acetabulum
options.D: Posterior and inferior glide of the femoral head in the acetabulum

questions.explanation: In hip flexion the convex femoral head spins and glides posteriorly (posteroinferiorly) in the acetabulum.
